settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Proxy service, client config, authentication and data retention.
settings.update.source.label: Update source
settings.proxy.port.label: Listen port
settings.proxy.port.desc: Default 23456. Auto-increments when the port is in use.
settings.proxy.bind.label: Listen address
settings.proxy.bind.desc: Default is loopback only. With "LAN accessible" on, other devices can point Claude Code at this machine's IP.
settings.proxy.bind.warning: ⚠️ When enabled, any device on the same network can reach the proxy. The proxy itself does no auth — be careful on untrusted networks.
settings.proxy.autostart.label: Launch at startup
settings.proxy.needsRestart: Proxy config changed (protocol/port/listen address/request body limit/HTTP/2). Restart the proxy service for it to take effect. In-flight requests are not interrupted.
settings.proxy.restart.applied: Proxy is running with the new config: {url}
settings.proxy.restart.shifted: Port {from} is in use; moved to {to}.
settings.proxy.restart.rolledBack: The new config could not take effect ({error}); restored the previous config.
settings.proxy.restart.notRun: Restart not performed: {error}. The previous config is still running.
settings.proxy.restart.webMove: After the restart this page will move to a new address. Continue?
settings.proxy.restart.webLockout: After the restart the proxy will listen on this machine only, and this device will no longer be able to reach the web UI. Continue?
settings.proxy.bodyLimit.label: Request body limit
settings.proxy.bodyLimit.desc: Maximum size of a single inbound request. Sessions with multiple base64 images (e.g. Codex with attachments) easily exceed a small limit and get rejected with 413. Click "Restart proxy service" to apply.
settings.proxy.mode.label: Listen protocol
settings.proxy.mode.desc: "HTTP only" is the simplest; "HTTPS only" requires importing the CA below into the system trust store; "both" exposes HTTP and HTTPS on separate ports so different clients can pick their own.
settings.proxy.httpsPort.label: HTTPS port
settings.proxy.httpsPort.desc: Default 23457. Auto-increments when the port is in use, and also steps around HTTP port conflicts.
settings.https.h2.label: HTTP/2 protocol
settings.https.h2.desc: When enabled, the HTTPS port advertises HTTP/2 via TLS ALPN — clients can negotiate h2, falling back to HTTP/1.1 on failure. When disabled, HTTP/1.1 is forced. Click "Restart proxy service" to apply.
settings.https.cert.fingerprint.label: CA fingerprint (SHA-256)
settings.https.cert.fingerprint.desc: Use this to verify the cert in your system trust store is the same CA. A matching fingerprint means the import succeeded.
settings.https.cert.export.label: Export CA certificate
settings.https.cert.export.desc: Export cc-router's self-signed CA public key. Both .pem and .crt are written (identical content). On Windows, double-click the .crt to launch the certificate install wizard; on macOS/Linux either .pem or .crt works. Once imported into the system trust store, browsers and clients will trust the localhost certificates cc-router issues.
settings.https.cert.exportOk: Exported both .pem and .crt of the CA. Follow the steps below to import it into your system trust store.
settings.https.cert.regenerateConfirm: Regenerate the leaf certificate? This does not affect the CA already imported into your trust store; the new cert takes effect immediately on the HTTPS port.
settings.https.cert.regenerateOk: Leaf certificate regenerated and in effect immediately.
settings.https.cert.sans.label: Extra SANs (IP / hostname)
settings.https.cert.sans.desc: One IP or hostname per line (e.g. 192.168.1.5 or my-laptop.local). localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1 are always in the cert — this list appends to them. The leaf cert regenerates when this field loses focus and takes effect immediately.
settings.https.cert.sans.regenerated: Leaf cert regenerated with the new SANs and in effect immediately.
settings.https.cert.howto.title: Import into the system trust store (one-time after export — every cert cc-router issues afterwards will be trusted)
settings.https.cert.howto.macos: Double-click the .pem → Keychain Access → select "cc-router local CA" → right-click "Get Info" → expand "Trust" → set "When using this certificate" to "Always Trust" → close the window and confirm with your password.
settings.https.cert.howto.windows: Double-click the .crt → Install Certificate → choose "Local Machine" (admin required) → "Place all certificates in the following store" → browse to "Trusted Root Certification Authorities" → Finish.
settings.https.cert.howto.linux: Copy the .crt to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/, then sudo update-ca-certificates. Firefox/Chromium use their own trust stores — import separately in browser settings.
settings.auth.token.label: Token authentication
settings.auth.token.desc: Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN to this token when launching Claude Code. After regenerating, every configured client must be updated.
settings.auth.token.enabled: Enabled — requests must carry a valid token
settings.auth.cors.label: CORS
settings.auth.cors.descEnabled: Enabled — responses carry CORS headers. Set a specific value like http://localhost:5173 to allow only that origin.
settings.auth.cors.descDisabled: Disabled — browser cross-origin calls will be blocked.
settings.auth.cors.statusDisabled: Disabled — browser cross-origin calls will be blocked
settings.webUi.enabled.label: Enable web UI
settings.webUi.enabled.desc: Serves the same management UI as the desktop app at /ui on the proxy port — open it in any browser. Takes effect immediately, no restart needed.
settings.webUi.auth.label: Login required
settings.webUi.auth.desc: The web UI signs in with the proxy access token; this switch is independent of “Token authentication” in the Security & Access tab.
settings.webUi.auth.on: Enabled — opening the web UI requires the token
settings.webUi.auth.off: Disabled — the web UI opens without signing in
settings.webUi.auth.confirmOff: Once disabled, any device that can reach this machine's proxy port can change subscriptions and settings without signing in. Disable anyway?
settings.webUi.auth.relogin: After saving, this page will need to sign in again.
settings.webUi.selfDisable.confirm: You are disabling the web UI from the web UI itself — this page will stop working immediately. Disable anyway?
settings.webUi.addresses.label: Access URLs
settings.webUi.addresses.localOnly: Currently reachable from this machine only; for LAN access, switch the listen address to 0.0.0.0 under “Proxy service” in the Proxy tab.
settings.webUi.warn.lanWithAuth: The management UI is exposed to the LAN; sign in with the proxy access token.
settings.webUi.warn.lanNoAuth: ⚠️ The web UI is exposed to the LAN with login disabled — any device that can reach this machine can change subscriptions and settings.
settings.tui.enabled.label: Enable terminal UI
settings.tui.enabled.desc: Lets the local cc-router-tui connect to and manage this app. Local connections only; the desktop app must stay running. Independent of “Web UI” above. Takes effect immediately, no restart needed.
settings.tui.launch.label: Launch command
settings.tui.launch.desc: Run the command below in a terminal.
settings.tui.launch.appimage: The AppImage path changes on every launch; this path is only valid for this run.
settings.tui.launch.missing: This build does not include the terminal UI binary.
settings.tui.launch.webHint: This is the path on the machine running cc-router.
settings.tui.launch.short: Already on PATH — use the short command above; the full path is below.
settings.tui.path.label: Add to PATH
settings.tui.path.desc.symlink: Creates a symlink to this app under /usr/local/bin, so cc-router-tui works from any terminal afterward. May prompt for your system password; no need to re-add after app updates.
settings.tui.path.desc.user_path: Adds the install directory to the current user's PATH, so cc-router-tui works from any terminal afterward. Already-open terminals need to be reopened to pick it up.
settings.tui.path.desc.copy: Copies a binary to ~/.local/bin, so cc-router-tui works from any terminal afterward. This copy doesn't follow app updates — click again after updating.
settings.tui.path.system: Installed with the system — cc-router-tui works from any terminal.
settings.tui.path.installedNote.user_pat: Already-open terminals need to be reopened to pick it up.
settings.tui.path.installedNote.copy: This copy doesn't follow app updates — click “Add to PATH” again after updating.
settings.tui.path.desktopOnly: Do this from the desktop app on the machine running cc-router.
settings.tui.path.blocked.translocated: cc-router is currently running straight from the download location, so this path is temporary. Move it to the Applications folder first, then reopen it.
settings.tui.path.blocked.on_disk_image: cc-router is still inside the disk image. Drag it to the Applications folder first, then reopen it.
settings.tui.path.blocked.occupied: {path} already exists and wasn't created by cc-router, so it won't be overwritten automatically.
settings.tui.path.localBinOffPath: ~/.local/bin isn't on your PATH. Add this line to your shell config (e.g. ~/.bashrc), then reopen your terminal:
settings.storage.retention.label: Request log retention
settings.storage.dbLimit.label: Database size limit
settings.storage.usage: Database is currently {size} · {requests} request log entries · {events} events. When the limit is exceeded, the oldest records are removed first; aggregated statistics and receipt data are not affected.
settings.language.label: UI language
settings.language.desc: Choose the cc-router UI display language. "Follow system" reads your system locale: Chinese → 中文, Japanese → 日本語, otherwise → English.
settings.appearance.theme.label: Theme
settings.appearance.theme.desc: Sketch is the hand-drawn notebook style of the website (default); Classic is the plain look from earlier versions; Win2000 is a retro Windows 2000 look
settings.appearance.mode.label: Color mode
settings.debug.mode.label: Debug mode
settings.debug.mode.desc: When on, every outbound request writes three .txt files to the debug-dumps directory: the client request body, cc-router's rewritten request body, and the upstream response body. Useful for protocol adaptation issues. Files contain full conversation content — turn off and clean up after debugging.
settings.debug.dumps.label: Dump directory
settings.debug.dumps.desc: Files accumulate over time; please clean up periodically.
settings.debug.open.webHint: The host directory can't be opened from the web UI; the path is debug-dumps under the app data directory.
settings.debug.clear.dialog.title: Clear debug-dumps?
settings.debug.clear.dialog.desc: This permanently deletes all .txt files under the debug-dumps directory. Samples you've already shared with Claude for debugging are safe to remove.
settings.backup.desc: Export your subscriptions and virtual model settings to a single file, then import it on another machine or after a reinstall. Request logs and statistics are not included.
backup.export.title: Export config
backup.export.includeSecrets: Include API keys and access token
backup.export.includeSecretsHint: Secrets are encrypted with a password you set. ChatGPT / Kiro sign-in credentials are never exported — sign in again on the new machine.
backup.export.webOnlyPlain: Secrets can only be exported from the desktop app.
backup.export.passwordTooShort: Password must be at least {min} characters
backup.export.passwordWarning: The password cannot be recovered. Without it you can still import the config, but not the secrets.
backup.export.copied: Copied to clipboard. Keep this password somewhere safe.
backup.export.copyFailed: Copy failed. Write this password down manually.
backup.import.title: Import config
backup.import.status.skip_oauth: Needs sign-in on this machine, skipped
backup.import.importToken: Also import the proxy access token
backup.import.importTokenHint: Replaces this machine's access token: Claude Code already configured here must switch to the new token, and the Web UI will need to sign in again.
backup.import.noSecretsHint: This file contains no secrets. Fill in the API key of each imported subscription before enabling it.
backup.import.report.skippedOauth: Sign in on this machine, then add these again: {names}
backup.import.report.skippedBindings: Bindings skipped for protocol mismatch (the subscriptions were still imported): {count}
backup.import.report.missingKey: Disabled until you fill in the API key: {names}
settings.danger.desc: Erase all subscriptions, API keys, virtual model bindings, request logs and settings. The app restarts into the initial welcome page. This cannot be undone.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: Project info & license
about.description: A local HTTP proxy that aggregates multiple LLM subscriptions into a single Anthropic Messages API endpoint, letting Claude Code switch between them transparently.
about.star.text: If cc-router helps you, consider giving it a Star on GitHub. It's the most direct way to encourage the author.
about.updater.debManual: · deb packages don't support in-place upgrade; please reinstall manually
about.updater.ready.title: Update ready
about.updater.ready.desc: Takes effect after restart. Restarting will briefly interrupt Claude Code's current session — do it at a convenient time.
about.disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
about.disclaimer.usage: This tool only switches between subscription plans you already own. Request bodies are passed through almost verbatim — no reverse engineering, no jailbreak, no circumvention. You are responsible for complying with each plan's terms of service. cc-router is intended for use with coding tools like Claude Code only; do not use it for anything else.
about.disclaimer.tos: Provider terms of service do not necessarily allow "routing a subscription key through a third-party proxy with multi-virtual-model dispatch" — especially for per-seat subscriptions like Coding Plans / Token Plans, where this pattern may trip risk controls. The author assumes no liability for any account being throttled, banned, or having its subscription cancelled as a result of using this tool.
about.disclaimer.warranty: This software is provided As-Is, without warranty of any kind. The author is not liable for any direct or indirect damages arising from its use, including but not limited to abnormal quota consumption, data loss, or business interruption.
about.disclaimer.affiliation: cc-router is an independent, third-party open-source project. It is not affiliated with, authorized or endorsed by Anthropic, and is not an official Claude / Claude Code application. Anthropic, Claude and Claude Code are trademarks of Anthropic, mentioned here only to indicate compatibility.

guide.codex.path.title: Codex CLI / Desktop config files
guide.codex.path.intro: Codex calls every model you've configured in cc-router through the /v1/responses entry: upstreams are translated automatically whether they speak the Anthropic or OpenAI protocol, and requests are dispatched by virtual model. Codex CLI and Codex Desktop share the same ~/.codex/ config, so editing it once covers both; this path only uses the HTTP port, no HTTPS or CA certificate needed. Edit the two files by hand in the three steps below.
guide.codex.config.title: Step 1: Edit config.toml
guide.codex.config.desc: Add the content below to config.toml (create the file if it doesn't exist). It registers a custom provider named cc-router (using the OpenAI Responses protocol) and a profile with the same name:
guide.codex.config.note1: If the file already has other settings, just append these two sections at the end. If you added [model_providers.cc-router] or [profiles.cc-router] before, delete the old sections first — TOML doesn't allow duplicate tables.
guide.codex.config.note2: base_url must end with /v1; Codex appends /responses to it. If Codex and cc-router are on different machines, replace 127.0.0.1 with the LAN IP of the machine running cc-router (set the listen address to 0.0.0.0 in Settings), and use the actual port shown on the Settings page.
guide.codex.configComment:
cc-router recommended config — generated by the cc-router setup guide
Usage: codex -p cc-router "your question"
Just save after editing; codex reads this file on its next launch
guide.codex.auth.title: Step 2: Edit auth.json
guide.codex.auth.desc: Replace the entire content of auth.json with the content below (create the file if it doesn't exist). OPENAI_API_KEY is your cc-router token — the same one Claude Code uses:
guide.codex.auth.note1: If you've signed in to Codex with a ChatGPT account, auth.json holds those official credentials. Make a copy of the original file before replacing it; to switch back to the official login later, rename the backup to its original name.
guide.codex.auth.note2: env_key = "OPENAI_API_KEY" in config.toml tells Codex to authenticate with this field; when cc-router auth is disabled, any value works. If you regenerate the token in Settings, come back here and copy it again.
guide.codex.auth.note3: This token grants access to all your upstream subscriptions, and auth.json stores it in plain text — don't share it or commit it to a code repository.
guide.codex.usage.title: Step 3: Launch Codex
guide.codex.usage.desc: In a terminal, launch Codex CLI with the cc-router profile via -p cc-router:
guide.codex.usage.desktop: Codex Desktop reads the same config: restart Codex Desktop once after editing, then pick the cc-router profile in the model picker.
guide.codex.slots.title: Use a different virtual model
guide.codex.slots.desc: The model field under [profiles.cc-router] in config.toml decides which virtual model is used. Change it to any of the following; Codex picks it up on its next launch:
guide.codex.slots.model-haiku: Haiku slot: tool calls, lightweight tasks
guide.codex.slots.note: Use cc-router's virtual model names here. Aliases such as gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.4 also work; see the model table on the "Generic Integration" tab for the mapping.
guide.codex.verify.title: Verify and troubleshoot
guide.codex.verify.desc1: Run one Codex conversation, then open
guide.codex.verify.desc2: : the Client column should show Codex CLI or Codex Desktop, the Virtual model column the matching slot, and the Real model column the upstream model the request was finally routed to.
guide.codex.trouble.title: Common issues
guide.codex.trouble.item1: 404 Not Found: base_url is missing the trailing /v1. cc-router's Responses entry is at /v1/responses.
guide.codex.trouble.item2: 401 Unauthorized: the token in auth.json doesn't match cc-router's current token (for example, it was regenerated). Come back to this page and copy the Step 2 content again.
guide.codex.trouble.item3: Requests don't go through cc-router: the CLI was launched without -p cc-router, or Codex Desktop wasn't restarted after the config change.
guide.codex.trouble.item4: Wrong model or model_not_found: the model field is misspelled. A misspelled name falls through to the fallback virtual model — use a virtual model name from the table above.
guide.codex.trouble.item5: Connection refused: the cc-router proxy isn't running, or the port in base_url doesn't match the actual port. Use the address shown at the top of this page.
guide.generic.intro: cc-router exposes four entry points: the first three are chat protocols that share the same subscriptions, virtual models, quotas and session affinity; the fourth, /v1/systemone, serves Jev decision models and only routes to model-jev. The "Entry" column in Request Logs shows which one each request came through. Pick the section matching the protocol your tool speaks.
guide.generic.tokenOff: Auth is disabled; any non-empty API key works.
guide.generic.messages.title: Anthropic Messages
guide.generic.messages.clients: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, OpenCode, OpenClaw, pi, Kimi code cli, etc.
guide.generic.messages.auth: x-api-key: <token> or Authorization: Bearer <token>, i.e. Claude Code's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.
guide.generic.messages.note1: This is the primary entry: requests pass through untouched with no protocol translation, so thinking, output_config.effort, cache_control, images and tool calls all work with native Anthropic semantics.
guide.generic.messages.note2: See the "Claude Code" tab for the full Claude Code setup; Claude Desktop needs local HTTPS, enable it under Settings → Proxy and follow the docs on the website.
guide.generic.messages.note3: Session affinity is keyed by the x-claude-code-session-id header first, then metadata.user_id.
guide.generic.messages.note4: Enabling "Forward client headers" on a subscription forwards whitelisted headers such as anthropic-beta / anthropic-version to that upstream verbatim. Per subscription, off by default.
guide.generic.responses.title: OpenAI Responses
guide.generic.responses.clients: Codex CLI, Codex Desktop App and other Responses clients
guide.generic.responses.auth: The token from the cc-router Settings page. Codex reads it from the OPENAI_API_KEY env var or ~/.codex/auth.json.
guide.generic.responses.authSnippetHint: ~/.codex/auth.json content (Codex reads OPENAI_API_KEY from here; your current token is filled in, any value works when auth is disabled):
guide.generic.responses.note1: Requests are translated to Anthropic Messages internally: instructions and developer messages merge into system, reasoning.effort maps to a thinking budget, and max_output_tokens maps to max_tokens (default 4096, raised automatically to cover the thinking budget).
guide.generic.responses.note2: Reasoning is bidirectional: upstream thinking comes back as a signed reasoning item; echo it back on the next turn to keep multi-turn reasoning context.
guide.generic.responses.note3: Image input is not supported, nor are OpenAI-only tools like file_search / web_search / computer_use; parallel_tool_calls is ignored.
guide.generic.responses.note4: Session affinity uses prompt_cache_key first, then the session_id header; Codex sends both.
guide.generic.responses.note5: For the full setup steps, see the "Codex" tab on this page.
guide.generic.chat.title: OpenAI Chat Completions
guide.generic.chat.clients: Open WebUI, Cherry Studio, Cline, LobeChat, etc.
guide.generic.chat.baseUrlHint: Some tools want it without /v1; follow the tool's hint.
guide.generic.chat.auth: The token from the cc-router Settings page (any non-empty value when auth is disabled).
guide.generic.chat.note1: Requests are translated to Anthropic Messages inside cc-router and go through the same scheduler, so subscriptions, virtual models, quotas and session affinity all apply; Request Logs show /v1/chat/completions as the entry.
guide.generic.chat.note2: Upstream thinking is returned in the reasoning_content field (the DeepSeek convention, collapsible in most clients); reasoning_content echoed back in history is dropped without affecting the conversation.
guide.generic.chat.note3: Images support both data: base64 and http(s) image_url; tool calls work in both directions; streaming responses always end with a usage frame.
guide.generic.chat.note4: Legacy functions / function_call fields are not supported and return 400; use tools / tool_choice instead.
guide.generic.chat.note5: n>1, logprobs and response_format JSON Schema enforcement are silently ignored.
guide.generic.chat.note6: Session affinity uses the user field first, then the x-session-id header, falling back to the first user message.
guide.generic.chat.note7: When a response contains tool calls, finish_reason is always tool_calls, so clients can rely on it to decide whether to run tools.
guide.generic.vm.prefixNote: Entries with * are fuzzy: claude-* matches any version suffix by prefix, gpt-*-<tier> matches the tier segment split on "-". All of them also accept an anthropic/ or openai/ prefix (LiteLLM style) with the same effect.
guide.generic.models.title: Model list
guide.generic.models.clients: Called automatically by Open WebUI, Cherry Studio and similar clients to fetch selectable models
guide.generic.models.authNone: Not required. This endpoint skips token validation so clients can fetch models right after entering the address.
guide.generic.models.format: Carries both the OpenAI and Anthropic list fields (object / data[] / has_more); each item has id, display_name, owned_by etc., so clients read whichever their protocol expects.
guide.generic.models.note1: The list is a fixed set of virtual model names and common aliases (30 entries) and does not change with your subscriptions; whether a name actually routes depends on the virtual model having subscriptions bound.
guide.generic.models.note2: Fuzzy patterns are not enumerated one by one; the list only includes representative aliases (e.g. claude-opus-4-7, gpt-5.6-terra).
guide.generic.systemone.title: Jev System One
guide.generic.systemone.clients: Your own code, agent frameworks, or anything that can send HTTP requests
guide.generic.systemone.urlHint: Use the full path /v1/systemone. Routing is decided by the path and always goes to model-jev.
guide.generic.systemone.modelHint: Just set model to model-jev in the request body: cc-router rewrites it to the Jev model configured on each subscription, or to that endpoint's example model if none is set (e.g. clef-flash, jev-latest), and the response still echoes model-jev. You can also use the upstream's real model name directly.
guide.generic.systemone.curlHint: Verify from the command line (current port and token already filled in):
guide.generic.systemone.note1: Passed through as-is with no protocol translation: the request body is {model, state, questions} and the response is {model, answers, usage}. Non-streaming only.
guide.generic.systemone.note2: Only subscriptions bound to model-jev whose endpoint is System One are used (TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Ollama 0.35+); chat subscriptions are never used here, and System One subscriptions never join the other virtual models.
guide.generic.systemone.note3: A 4xx from one upstream moves on to the next (their validation rules differ slightly). If all of them fail, a request error returns the last upstream's error as-is; anything else returns 503.
guide.generic.systemone.note4: Session affinity only uses the x-session-id header; without it, requests are assigned round-robin.
guide.generic.systemone.note5: These models don't generate text, so chat tools such as Claude Code can't use them; the chat entry points return 400 for model-jev.

guide.hermes.config.desc: Write the content below into the config file. Filled in with cc-router's current port, ready to use.
guide.hermes.auth.title: API Key configuration
guide.hermes.auth.desc: Use the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable, or run hermes auth add anthropic --type api-key --api-key <token>. The token is shown and regenerated on the Settings page.
guide.hermes.note.apiMode: api_mode must be anthropic_messages (the option in Hermes that matches cc-router's protocol). Anything else mismatches the protocol and 4xx's everything.
guide.opencode.path.title: Config file path
guide.opencode.path.note: Pick either project-level opencode.json or the global ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json.
guide.opencode.config.title: Config example
guide.opencode.config.desc: The @ai-sdk/anthropic npm package declares this as an Anthropic-protocol endpoint. Filled in with cc-router's current port and token, ready to use.
guide.opencode.note.baseUrlTrap: ⚠️ Don't append /v1 to baseURL. @ai-sdk/anthropic auto-appends /v1/messages internally, so doubling up gives /v1/v1/messages → 404 (this is the cause of OpenCode issue #5163).
guide.opencode.note.usage: Use /models and pick cc-router/model-opus (or sonnet / haiku).
stats.title: Statistics
stats.subtitle: Aggregated view of usage, latency and success rate. Rolled up by local calendar day and kept permanently — unaffected by log retention cleanup.
stats.section.yearSub: Last 365 days, independent of the time range below.
stats.section.periodSub: Every number and chart below uses the same time range.
stats.error.load: Failed to load. Use the refresh button in the top-right to retry.
stats.kpi.cacheReadHint: Cache read ÷ (input + cache read + cache write). OpenAI / Gemini upstreams already include cached tokens in input, so this reads low for them.
stats.heatmap.title: Token usage heatmap

stats.daily.hourlySubtitle: Today's request volume per hour, stacked by outcome.
stats.daily.empty: No requests in the selected range.

stats.daily.tokenHourlySubtitle: Today's tokens per hour, light to dark: cache read / cache write / input / output.

stats.kpi.toolShareHint: Requests that made at least one tool call ÷ successful requests. The more agentic your sessions, the higher this gets.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.subtitle: Each subscription is one vendor's API key. Status reflects health checks live.
subscriptions.empty.message: No subscriptions yet. Click "Add subscription" to get started.
virtualModels.title: Virtual models
virtualModels.subtitle1: Four fixed virtual models map to Claude Code's model slots;
virtualModels.subtitle2: is the catch-all — any other model request goes here. model-jev only serves POST /v1/systemone.
virtualModels.mode.label: Mode
virtualModels.mode.sequentialHint: By priority, fail over on error
virtualModels.mode.stickyHint: Same session pins the same subscription, round-robin across sessions; keeps the prompt cache warm, concurrent subagents share it, and re-pins automatically on failure
virtualModels.addButton: Add subscription to this virtual model
virtualModels.dialog.title: Select subscriptions to add
virtualModels.dialog.empty: No available subscriptions. Add one in "Subscriptions" first.
virtualModels.jev.keyHint: Use your cc-router access token as the API key
virtualModels.dialog.emptyJev: No System One subscriptions available. Add one in "Subscriptions" first (the System One endpoint of Ollama / OpenRouter, or TypeSafe).
virtualModels.dialog.needFallbackSlot: Set a fallback model in the subscription first
virtualModels.dialog.search: Search name, provider, host or model
virtualModels.dialog.unused: Not used by any virtual model yet
subscriptionNew.title: Add subscription
subscriptionNew.importBackupHint: Have a config file exported from cc-router?
subscriptionNew.welcomeSubtitle: Add your first subscription. We'll bind it to all 4 virtual models and jump to the setup guide.
subscriptionNew.subtitle: Connect a vendor's API key to the router and bind it to virtual model slots.
subscriptionNew.customHint: Custom path: fill in connection info and model slots in one page, no two-step wizard.
subscriptionNew.customGeminiHint: Use this for Google AI Studio or any Gemini-compatible relay. cc-router translates Anthropic Messages calls into Gemini generateContent automatically.
subscriptionNew.geminiBaseUrlHint: Gemini endpoint domain root. Use https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com for AI Studio, or your relay's actual domain.
subscriptionNew.geminiMessagesPathHint: URL path template. Must contain the {model} placeholder — cc-router substitutes it with the slot's real model name per request.
subscriptionNew.geminiAuthLocked: Gemini endpoints always use the x-goog-api-key header. Just paste your API key, no auth method to pick.
subscriptionNew.customGeminiInteractions: Use this for Google's new Interactions API (/v1beta/interactions) or a compatible relay. cc-router translates Anthropic Messages calls into Interactions automatically. Unlike the older generateContent endpoint above, the model goes in the request body, so no {model} placeholder is needed.
subscriptionNew.geminiInteractionsBaseUr: Interactions endpoint domain root. Use https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com for AI Studio, or your relay's actual domain.
subscriptionNew.geminiInteractionsMessag: URL path, fixed at /v1beta/interactions. The model goes in the request body — no {model} placeholder needed.
subscriptionNew.geminiInteractionsAuthLo: Interactions endpoints always use the x-goog-api-key header. Just paste your API key, no auth method to pick.
subscriptionNew.customOpenaiHint: Use this for the official OpenAI /v1/responses endpoint or any OpenAI-compatible relay (one-api, new-api, etc.). cc-router translates Anthropic Messages into OpenAI Responses calls and supports multi-turn reasoning replay.
subscriptionNew.openaiAuthLocked: OpenAI Responses endpoints always use Authorization: Bearer. Just paste your API key (usually starts with sk-...), no auth method to pick.
subscriptionNew.openaiBaseUrlHint: OpenAI Responses endpoint domain root. Use https://api.openai.com for the official API, or your relay's actual domain.
subscriptionNew.openaiMessagesPathHint: URL path, usually /v1/responses. Relays may use a different path — check their docs.
subscriptionNew.customOpenaiChatHint: Use this for OpenAI /v1/chat/completions compatible services: DeepSeek, Together, Groq, Ollama, any one-api / new-api relay, and OpenAI's legacy models (GPT-4 / 4-turbo). cc-router translates Anthropic Messages into Chat Completions calls automatically, and surfaces DeepSeek R1's reasoning_content as Claude Code thinking blocks.
subscriptionNew.openaiChatBaseUrlHint: Chat Completions endpoint domain root. Examples: OpenAI https://api.openai.com, DeepSeek https://api.deepseek.com, Together https://api.together.xyz, Groq https://api.groq.com/openai, Ollama http://localhost:11434.
subscriptionNew.openaiChatMessagesPathHi: URL path, usually /v1/chat/completions. Relays may use a different path — check their docs.
subscriptionNew.openaiChatAuthLocked: OpenAI Chat Completions endpoints always use Authorization: Bearer. Just paste your API key (usually starts with sk-...; for auth-free setups like Ollama, any non-empty string works), no auth method to pick.
subscriptionNew.errGeminiPathPlaceholder: Gemini path template must contain the {model} placeholder
subscriptionNew.providerNameHint: Name shown in the dropdown — editable later.
subscriptionNew.baseUrlHint: Domain root only — do not include the /v1/messages path.
subscriptionNew.messagesPathHint: Usually /v1/messages. Some proxies use a different path.
subscriptionNew.noteHint: Local label only — never uploaded anywhere.
subscriptionNew.slotsHint: Slots determine which real model cc-router routes model-fable / model-opus / model-sonnet / model-haiku to. After filling in the URL and API key, click "Fetch model list" to pick from a dropdown — if the list can't be fetched, you can still type model names manually.
subscriptionNew.errFillProvider: Please enter the provider display name
subscriptionNew.errFillNote: Please enter a note for the subscription
subscriptionNew.errFillSlots: Please enter a real model name for all four slots (Fable / Opus / Sonnet / Haiku)
oauth.chatgpt.title: Connect ChatGPT account
oauth.chatgpt.subtitle: Use the Codex quota of your ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription. Authorization is independent from the Codex CLI and stored only inside cc-router.
oauth.chatgpt.instructions: Browser opened. Please confirm the code shown on the page matches the one below, then authorize.
oauth.chatgpt.waitingForAuth: Waiting for you to authorize in the browser…
oauth.chatgpt.connectHint: After authorization, cc-router will run Claude Code using your ChatGPT subscription quota. Your local Codex CLI is not affected.
oauth.chatgpt.tosWarning: ⚠️ ChatGPT subscriptions are intended for OpenAI's own products and the Codex CLI; third-party usage is a gray area and OpenAI reserves the right to apply account controls. Tips: use a secondary account; avoid bursty high-frequency calls; phone-number verification when authorizing a new device is the standard flow.
oauth.kiro.title: Connect Kiro account
oauth.kiro.subtitle: Use the free Claude quota from Kiro IDE (backed by AWS CodeWhisperer).
oauth.kiro.tosWarning: ⚠️ Kiro subscriptions are intended for Kiro IDE / kiro-cli usage; third-party access is a gray area and AWS reserves the right to apply account controls. Tips: avoid bursty high-frequency calls; phone-number verification when authorizing a new device is the standard flow.
oauth.kiro.importDescription: If you have logged in to Kiro IDE or run kiro-cli login, your credentials are already cached under ~/.aws/sso/cache/ and can be loaded directly.
oauth.kiro.deviceFlowDescription: Use AWS SSO OIDC Device Flow to complete Builder ID authorization in your browser (a free account is enough). On success cc-router receives the refresh_token automatically; it never enters JS.
oauth.kiro.deviceInstructions: Browser opened. Please confirm the code shown on the page matches the one below, then authorize.
oauth.kiro.waitingForAuth: Waiting for you to authorize in the browser…
oauth.kiro.connectHint: Supports either importing Kiro IDE's cached JSON or AWS Builder ID OAuth. After import you still need to confirm 4 disguise fields.
oauth.kiro.profileArnDetected: ✓ profileArn detected, will be injected on each request.
oauth.kiro.disguiseHint: These fields are sent to AWS together with the user-agent / x-amz-user-agent header on every request, mimicking a Kiro IDE client. Defaults follow cc-router upgrades; you can edit them manually (e.g. copy the real IDE's machineId to further reduce risk-control friction).
subscriptionEdit.endpointChangeWarn: Saving will re-copy connection info from this endpoint template
subscriptionEdit.requiredHeadersHint: Custom request headers attached to every forwarded request, e.g. routing headers required by enterprise gateways. Overrides default headers with the same name. Use "Test connection" after saving to verify.
subscriptionEdit.forwardClientHeadersHin: When enabled, the client's x-claude-code-session-id, anthropic-beta, anthropic-version, x-app and x-stainless-* headers are forwarded to the upstream as-is (relays can use them for per-session rate limiting). Credentials and User-Agent are never forwarded; forwarding anthropic-beta may enable the corresponding beta features upstream. Off by default.
testConnection.noTestModel: This subscription has no model slots configured and no example model to fall back on, so it can't be tested
lastError.upstreamQuotaExhausted: Upstream quota exhausted (5-hour or monthly quota)
subscriptionEdit.keyDialog.title: Update API key
subscriptionEdit.keyDialog.desc: The new key takes effect immediately.
subscriptionEdit.deleteDialog.refByOutro: After deletion these virtual models will lose this subscription.
subscriptionEdit.deleteDialog.noRef: Deleting a subscription also removes the stored API key.
subscriptionBalance.title: Balance
subscriptionBalance.neverFetched: Not fetched yet — click the button to load the latest balance
subscriptionBalance.accountUnavailable: Account is currently unavailable (out of credit or restricted)
subscriptionBalance.entry.label: Balance ({unit})
quota.title: Usage quota
quota.desc: A safety valve on the cc-router side: once any period hits its limit, the subscription is paused from scheduling and resumes automatically in the next period. Counts all four token kinds (input / output / cache write / cache read).
quota.resetTotalConfirm: Reset the lifetime total counter to zero? This cannot be undone.
quota.noLimits: No quota set. Once configured above, per-period usage shows here.

modelSlot.fable.label: Fable slot
modelSlot.opus.label: Opus slot
modelSlot.sonnet.label: Sonnet slot
modelSlot.haiku.label: Haiku slot
modelSlot.fallback.label: Fallback slot (optional)
modelSlot.fallback.hint: When the fallback virtual model routes to this subscription, the request model is rewritten to this value; leave empty to pass unknown models through unchanged (translation-based subscriptions like Kiro / Codex must set this to participate in fallback)
modelSlot.jev.label: Jev model (optional)
modelSlot.jev.hint: When model-jev routes to this subscription, the request model is rewritten to this value; if empty, a request for model-jev uses this endpoint's example model and any other name is passed through unchanged
modelSlot.historicalTitle: {model} is not in the auto list — it may be a previously manual entry. Switch to manual mode to change it.
modelSlot.modelIdPh: Enter the model ID provided by the vendor
slotEffort.hint: The dropdown on the right sets the reasoning effort for this slot. "Auto" passes through whatever effort the Claude Code request carries; picking a specific level ignores the client value and forces that level (useful for models that only accept a single level).
slotEffort.unsupportedKiro: The Kiro / CodeWhisperer upstream protocol has no reasoning field, so reasoning effort cannot be set. If you need reasoning, use an OpenAI / Codex / Gemini style provider instead.

receipts.title: Receipts
receipts.subtitle: Render your subscription token usage as a shareable receipt-style snapshot. Pricing is hidden by default — only usage is shown.
receipts.print.title: Print receipt
receipts.controls.display.title: Display options
receipts.controls.display.theme.label: Receipt theme
receipts.controls.display.theme.desc: Themed receipts use a fixed layout (labels in each theme's local language). The detail options and view modes below only apply to the classic themes; theme fonts load on demand from public CDNs and fall back to system fonts offline.
receipts.controls.display.showProviderLo: Add brand icons (Anthropic / DeepSeek / Zhipu, etc.) before the provider name on each sub-item row. Auto-grayscaled in monochrome mode.
receipts.controls.display.showCacheDesc: Hide to keep only the input / output rows for a cleaner slip.
receipts.controls.display.showCountsDesc: Hide to show only token counts; the "156×" suffix on each item disappears.
receipts.controls.display.compactTokensD: Compress token numbers into K/M form (e.g. 12.35K, 1.23M); values below 1000 stay as-is.
receipts.controls.display.groupMode.desc: Switch the slip body's aggregation dimension; By subscription / Totals only no longer group by virtual-model slot.
receipts.controls.display.footerCode.des: Style of the site code at the bottom of the receipt; barcodes use Code128.
receipts.controls.filter.title: Filters
receipts.controls.filter.excludeDeletedD: When checked, the receipt hides usage from subscriptions that have been deleted; totals recalculate automatically.
receipts.controls.export.title: Export receipt
receipts.controls.export.printAnimationD: A receipt printer prints the slip out — about 2 seconds, skip anytime.
liveRouting.title: Live routing
liveRouting.subtitle: Which AI agent a request comes from, which virtual model it lands on, and which subscription finally serves it — all in one picture. This page is read-only.

liveRouting.clientAccess.retention: Detection window = log retention ({days} days). A client whose logs have already been purged shows as not connected.
liveRouting.clientAccess.retentionForeve: Request logs are kept forever, so the detection window covers the full history.

liveRouting.api.systemone: Jev decision protocol (System One), routes only to model-jev
